sources.title: A Community Kitchen Closing Routine
sources.author: Dual Dictionary project — AI-assisted original source
sources.article: Volunteers at River Street community kitchen share a simple closing routine. Two people take turns checking the refrigerator temperatures and noting the results on a daily sheet. Each volunteer is responsible for one part of the room: the preparation table, serving counter, or dish area. Before leaving, put sealed ingredients back in labelled storage and wipe work surfaces with the approved cleaner. If a label is missing, do not guess what is inside; place the container in the marked review tray and ask the shift lead. The lead checks the closing sheet at 7 p.m. and leaves a short message about anything that needs attention before the next team arrives. New volunteers can ask for a demonstration during handover.

sources.title: Comparing Shade Along Two City Routes
sources.author: Dual Dictionary project — AI-assisted original source
sources.article: A university geography group is comparing afternoon temperatures along two city walking routes. The researchers record shade coverage, the percentage of each route shaded by trees or buildings, beside every surface-temperature reading. To make a fair comparison, observers visit both routes at the same time on several clear days. The first set of measurements is a provisional estimate because one sensor stopped working during the second visit. The team will check the missing interval against field notes before calculating a weekly average. A single hot afternoon cannot show that one route is usually warmer. The final report will describe the method, identify limitations and include the route map so another group can repeat the survey.

sources.title: Reporting a Lost Item at the Station
sources.author: Dual Dictionary project — AI-assisted original source
sources.article: Passengers who find a wallet or bag at Central Station should hand it in to the information desk rather than leave it on a seat. Staff attach a numbered tag and record the time and location where the item was found. A person collecting it may need to give proof of ownership, such as a clear description of an item inside, before staff release it. The desk stores small objects in a locked cabinet and keeps larger bags in a supervised room. Items are recorded in a daily register so the next shift can answer questions. If a passenger thinks they have lost something, they should describe it without sharing sensitive account numbers in public. The station will contact the owner if a safe contact detail is available.
